backtest.text: Backtest (run in 2013–2019 on every filer's data as of then, 2,274 outcomes, without analysts' consensus): the 80% range of revenue three years out held 80% of what happened (11% fell below it, 9% above) — about right. That is with every regime's growth spread × 1.5, the one number fitted on these outcomes (and used here): as the hidden Markov model estimates them, the range held 68% (18% below, 14% above) — a single year's regime spread understates how far revenue can drift over several.

methods.formula: Value = (assets in place + C − net debt) ÷ shares;  C = S·N(d₁) − K·e^(−rT)·N(d₂), d₁ = [ln(S ÷ K) + (r + σ²/2)T] ÷ σ√T, d₂ = d₁ − σ√T
steps: S = the expansion in year 5: the revenue it adds $789.5M (to $1.38B) × margin 21.9% × (1 − tax), as a growing perpetuity, discounted = $1.38B
K = capital to build it: $789.5M ÷ sales-to-capital 0.29 = $2.73B
σ = 42% (its stock, a year of daily closes), T = 5 years, r = 4.91% → C = $320.4M
assets in place = NOPAT $114.1M ÷ WACC = $1.30B; value = ($1.30B + $320.4M − net debt $826.9M) ÷ 93,688,471 = $8.51
assumptions: an assumption: the business is riskier than the market sees only through its price

methods.fit: It is loss-making or growing fast: much of its value is the chance to become a larger, profitable business, which behaves like an option — worth more the more uncertain it is.
